claims.text: DeepSeek released Harness (CLI alias `dsh`), an open-source agent-runtime framework for building and running coding agents, on GitHub on 13 August 2026, in developer preview
claims.reasoning: GitHub API (repos/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) confirms org deepseek-ai (id 148330874, matches DeepSeek's known org), created_at 2026-08-13T11:56:32Z, not a fork, not archived. README verbatim states developer-preview status and warns of breaking changes. DeepSeek's own X post (retrieved via search snippet, direct fetch blocked HTTP 402) independently uses matching language ('v0.1 is now available in Developer Preview'). Independently reported beyond DeepSeek's own channels by The New Stack (Frederic Lardinois, 2026-08-13).

claims.text: The Harness codebase is released under the MIT license
claims.reasoning: Verified at the byte level: LICENSE file fetched raw (both via web and base64-decoded from the GitHub API by the falsifier independently) reads standard MIT text, 'Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek'. GitHub API license.spdx_id = MIT. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md exists for dependency disclosure (normal for MIT projects with dependencies, not a carve-out); its contents were not fetched, so a restrictive sub-component cannot be fully ruled out, but the top-level LICENSE covering the codebase is unambiguous.

claims.text: Harness's architecture implements models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, filesystems, the agent loop, orchestration and the UI as swappable plugins
claims.reasoning: This is DeepSeek's own description, appearing independently and near-verbatim in both the GitHub README (fetched raw) and DeepSeek's own X announcement -- not a VentureBeat paraphrase.

claims.text: DeepSeek's own release materials make no comparison to any competitor; press coverage framing Harness as a rival to Anthropic's coding tools disagrees on which product
claims.reasoning: Direct read of the GitHub README and DeepSeek's X post found zero mentions of Anthropic, Claude Code, or Claude Cowork. VentureBeat's headline says 'rival to Claude Code'; TechNode's headline instead frames it against 'Claude Cowork', a different, verified-real Anthropic product launched January 2026. Two outlets naming two different rivals is itself evidence the comparison is each outlet's own framing, not sourced from DeepSeek. Labeled single-source/press-framing rather than a confirmed DeepSeek claim; article attributes it explicitly to press coverage.
